noveltyJustification: Three findings are new implementation facts (exact-match reserved IDs, HTML-tag scan, cleaned-label length) and ten refine iterations 12-13; (3 + 0.5*10) / 13 = 0.615.

label: The rule list grows from seven bullets to nine and the first-six check split must be recalculated, or the gate is misdescribed.
Proposed constants are MAX_LABEL 80, an emoji regex, a four-word reserved set, an anchored subgraph regex and an HTML-tag regex beside the existing block.
Reserved IDs should be matched exactly, not case-insensitively, because Mermaid keywords are lowercase and End is a legal ID.
Edge condition: reject non-solid style, undirected and bidirectional connectors in the existing edge loop with one message naming the meaning.
The raw markup scan must match HTML tags and emphasis, never a bare angle bracket, because arrows contain both characters.
Emoji checks belong on cleaned node and edge labels, since emoji survive cleaning and both render the same way.
Label length should be measured after cleaning, because the cleaned label is what renders on the board.
Underscore stays an error and camelCase stays unenforced, keeping the checker's binary exit contract.
Subgraph rejection is a raw-text condition anchored at line start, with no nesting count because every subgraph is rejected.
Eight planted models prove the new rules: emoji, reserved ID, underscore, 81 characters, undirected edge, dashed edge, subgraph and HTML tag.
The good fixture and all five shipped patterns survive, since the longest label is 27 characters and none uses a dashed edge or subgraph.
Label length and emoji fold into the existing label bullet, keeping nine bullets instead of eleven.
The checker docstring enumerates the rules and must be updated with the rule list or it becomes the next stale mirror.

reason: It needs a warning channel and a non-binary exit code the checker does not have.
